text: In Taylor's theorem about x = a, the Lagrange form of the remainder after the degree-n term is:
choices: f^{(n)}(c)/n! * (x-a)^n for some c between a and x
f^{(n+1)}(c)/(n+1)! * (x-a)^{n+1} for some c between a and x
f^{(n+1)}(c)/n! * (x-a)^{n+1} for some c between a and x
explanation: The Lagrange remainder evaluates the (n+1)-st derivative at an intermediate point c and carries (n+1)! with (x-a)^{n+1}. Option 1 is merely the n-th term of the series, option 2 wrongly evaluates the derivative at a, and option 4 uses the wrong factorial n! instead of (n+1)!.
